subject.title: Browser-opened temporary tabs/windows should close automatically after task completion

question: Should OpenClaw close primary-agent browser tabs at every normal task completion, and what ownership rule defines a temporary tab?
rationale: Current docs and code intentionally keep active primary-session tabs reusable until idle/cap/reset cleanup, while the requested default can surprise users unless run ownership and preservation are explicit.

options.title: Ownership-based default cleanup
options.body: Close only tabs created for the completed run and preserve explicitly kept, pinned, or user-owned pages; this matches the linked FSB design input and is the recommended direction.

options.title: Keep idle/cap/reset cleanup only
options.body: Treat the existing cleanup model as the intended product boundary and close this request as not planned after documenting that active primary tabs remain reusable.

options.title: Add opt-in close-after-task mode
options.body: Introduce a compatibility-sensitive opt-in mode after deciding the config shape and upgrade behavior, leaving the current default unchanged.

recommendation.title: Ownership-based default cleanup
recommendation.body: Close only tabs created for the completed run and preserve explicitly kept, pinned, or user-owned pages; this matches the linked FSB design input and is the recommended direction.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored both the idle browser cleanup feature and the merged peer-reset cleanup, so he has the strongest history for deciding the remaining behavior contract.
